chapter_title: The Chapter of the Three Seasons

fills.notes: After the victory the text locates the sons remaining behind “in the worlds … in the …”: in the oldest Iranian-Manichaean substrate, the Darkness is structured as “worlds/realms” articulated as the five dark abysses. This is the standard correspondential geography (depths = degrees of obscuration).
Parallel to “went down to the abyss” and to later “swept the waste to the abyss”; the sons are said to remain in the abyssal regions of Darkness.
The clause “until he shall catch all of them … he bound them all up” needs a temporal hinge moving from their remaining-behind to the subsequent binding/capturing.
The immediate referent of ‘great victory’ in this season is the initial combat with the King and powers of Darkness; the substrate register states victory in structural terms, not moral exhortation.
Transition: “until he prevailed … he fulfilled the will …” requires a completion marker; the sense is endurance across ‘lifetimes and generations’ culminating in fulfillment.

“They set in order the things of the universe, they set up …” in the second season is the construction of the ordered heavens/structures (firmaments) as intermediates between Light and the mixed world.
Balanced repetition: “set in order … set in order … the universe” invites a totalizing object (“all the universe / all its orders”).
“up to the moment when they go out … it was reckoned” describes completion of arranging and withdrawing to their proper stations/regions; ‘places’ fits the impersonal cosmological register.
¶5 continues the sequence of the second season into the third agent’s operation; an adverbial handoff (“afterwards”) plus an ordering-verb matches the chapter’s structuring by phases.

The line “the universe …” naturally takes the passive result of prior ordering: the cosmos becomes ‘purified/clarified’ as mixture is sorted. This anticipates the Ambassador’s later purification work.
“The Third Ambassador spread … that is in the … living” corresponds to the Ambassador’s function of eliciting/separating Light by a ‘net’/‘snare’ display (a technical image for extraction).
The phrase “that is in the … living” needs a locative/qualifying genitive; ‘region’ keeps the substrate cosmographic tone (zones/regions) rather than devotional phrasing.

After “he … he separated beauty” a verb of manifestation fits: the Ambassador’s appearance causes the beautiful/light to be drawn out. A simple ‘shone’ is correspondentially apt (light revealing light).
After sweeping waste to the abyss, the remaining operation is stabilization of the mixed construction: the world is ‘set/caused to stand’ as an ordered container for further separation.
“Sin came … from the darkness” expects “up/out” movement (eruption from lower degree to confront the revealed image).
With ‘from the darkness’ the natural complement is emergence ‘out’ (opposite of descent).
¶8 compares durations and explicitly refers to “the time that the First Man spent in the world of darkness”; the subject that “lasts long” is therefore the first season/period.
The argument is a comparative calculation: ‘if you should say that … it is small’—the natural item under debate is the duration of the first period (First Man’s sojourn).
He instructs them in proportional comparison: “if you should … to him … and you consult … you will tell him: Twenty times!”; ‘compare it’ fits the mathematical/ratiological tone.
“and you consult … you will tell him” requires an object: consult ‘another’ (reckoning/measure) for a second ratio.
“It is greater again in this other one” is the needed connective/adverb to mark a second step in the proportional series.
The sentence “Less also is this other one …” contrasts the third measure against the middle; the chapter repeatedly names the ‘intermediate’ (second) season as shorter.

The following clause moves to what happens during the long span: reception of the fruit/seed from trees, years, generations, and ascent of portions of earth/light; a temporal frame ‘for in that time’ fits.
“people will receive the {} of the trees” in this mythic cycle is the taking of fruit/seed producing bodies and generations (a natural correspondence of propagation in the mixed world).

fills.fill: it is greater than the intermediate season
fills.notes: ¶12 resumes the triadic comparison: first > third; third > second. The lacuna stands where the comparative to the second season is expected before recalling “when the Father of Life and the Mother of Life shaped the universe.”
Closing summary formula: “These are the … three periods of time that occur” regularly uses ‘reckoned/counted’ in this chapter’s register of measurement.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained at the level of cosmological function (three seasons; ordering of the cosmos; Ambassador’s extraction; eruption of Sin). Exact Coptic phrasing is less recoverable in ¶10 and parts of ¶5–¶4 where the underlying text likely had technical terms; restorations there are correspondentially consistent but remain tentative.
